tagline: Switch to the Murmur keyboard. Speak. It types.
description: Native iOS Murmur: a SwiftUI app plus a custom keyboard extension, sharing the desktop app's formatter brains through spec files in shared/. Apple forbids microphone access inside keyboard extensions, so dictation uses the containing-app bounce that Wispr Flow proved: the keyboard's mic key opens the Murmur app, the app records and transcribes through the same Groq pipeline as desktop, and the finished text returns to the keyboard through the App Group container. Action Button and Siri Shortcut triggers reduce the keyboard-switching friction.

stack.keyboard: Custom keyboard extension (UIInputViewController), dictation-first layout, not a full QWERTY in v1
stack.transcription: Groq audio/transcriptions (whisper-large-v3-turbo) or any OpenAI-compatible base URL, same as desktop
stack.formatting: Groq chat/completions driven by shared/format-spec.json, fail-open, same as desktop
stack.sharing: App Group container for keyboard-app data, murmur:// URL scheme for the bounce
stack.verification: xcodebuild test on the iOS Simulator is the smoke equivalent; unit tests mirror the desktop smoke checks with shared test vectors

conventions.definitionOfDone: A story passes only when every acceptance criterion is verified. Criteria needing a physical iPhone, a live microphone, a real API key, or App Store Connect are verified manually by Labroi and noted in notes.
conventions.process: Work stories in priority order. Keep xcodebuild test green, and keep the desktop's npm run smoke green whenever shared/ or src/ is touched. After completing a story, set passes=true, record how it was verified in notes, run npm run roadmap, and commit. git pull --rebase before every commit: parallel sessions run on other machines.

hardConstraints: The keyboard extension never touches the microphone. Apple forbids it; all audio lives in the containing app.
The API key lives in the iOS Keychain, is shared to no extension, and never appears in the repo, UserDefaults, or logs.
Audio goes only to the configured API; transcripts and history stay on device; the App Group carries only what the keyboard needs.
The formatter fails open: a dictation is never lost because the cleanup LLM errored or chatted.
No binary assets in the repo: iOS icons are generated by script into the asset catalog.
The keyboard extension stays lean: no networking libraries, no audio frameworks, well under the extension memory ceiling.
Night studio design system: ink surfaces, warm text, amber reserved for live states, red for record and errors.
shared/format-spec.json is the single source of truth for formatter rules on every platform.

stories.title: Shared formatter spec
stories.description: As a maintainer, the formatter rules (levels, styles, structure, numbers, chat-guard tells) live in shared/format-spec.json, and both the desktop app and iOS build their prompts from it, so tuning once ships everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: shared/format-spec.json holds the level rules, style rules, structure rules, number rules, base rules, and chat-guard tell phrases currently hardcoded in src/main/transcribe.js

Desktop transcribe.js composes its prompt from the spec file with behavior byte-identical to before (existing formatPrompt, structurePrompt, numberPrompt, formatChatGuard smoke checks unchanged and green)
A new required desktop smoke check (specDriven) proves the prompt changes when the spec file changes, so the wiring cannot silently regress to constants
shared/test-vectors.json captures the correction, expansion, and chat-guard cases the desktop smoke checks use, so iOS unit tests consume the identical vectors
npm run smoke green on desktop after the refactor
stories.notes: Verified 2026-07-23. shared/format-spec.json now holds header, rules label, spoken commands, footer, dictionary and corrections rule templates, vocabulary prompt, all five levels, structure rules, both styles, number rules, chat-guard tells plus thresholds, and the silence no_speech_prob threshold. transcribe.js composes from the spec (buildFormatPrompt, guardFormatOutput, extractTranscript take an optional spec arg defaulting to the file). Byte-identical proven by snapshotting all 72 level x style x numbers prompt combos before the refactor and diffing after: zero mismatches. specDriven required check proves the default prompt contains strings read from the file on disk and that a mutated spec changes the output, so a regression to constants fails smoke. shared/test-vectors.json carries the correction, expansion, chat-guard, and silence-segment cases; new required sharedVectors check runs every vector through the real desktop implementations. shared/**/* added to builder files so packaged apps ship the spec. npm run smoke green: all 26 required checks true including specDriven and sharedVectors, formatPrompt, structurePrompt, numberPrompt, formatChatGuard untouched and green.

stories.title: Xcode project, app shell, and project law
stories.description: As a developer, ios/ contains a working Xcode project: the Murmur SwiftUI app and the keyboard extension target, an App Group linking them, generated icons, and a unit test target that is the smoke equivalent.
acceptanceCriteria: ios/ Xcode project builds the app and keyboard extension targets cleanly via xcodebuild from a fresh clone
App target and keyboard target share an App Group; bundle identifiers are consistent (com.labroi.murmur.ios and a keyboard child id)
xcodebuild test runs a unit test target on the iOS Simulator and passes; this command is documented in CLAUDE.md as the iOS verification gate
App icons and the keyboard icon are generated by a script (no binary assets committed); the asset catalog consumes the generated files, and generation is documented
Night studio design tokens (ink, panel, warm text, amber, red, mono) defined once in Swift and used by the app shell
The murmur:// URL scheme is registered and routes into the app
stories.notes: Verified 2026-07-23 on Xcode 26.6, iOS 26.5 simulator. Hand-authored pbxproj (objectVersion 77, synchronized folder groups) with three targets: Murmur app, MurmurKeyboard extension, MurmurTests hosted unit tests. xcodebuild -scheme Murmur -destination iPhone 17 build succeeds with the appex embedded and validated; xcodebuild test runs 10 tests, all pass (spec and vector bundles, defaults, thresholds, murmur:// route parsing, App Group container resolution). Gate documented in CLAUDE.md, device name updated to a simulator that exists (iPhone 16 does not ship with Xcode 26). Bundle ids com.labroi.murmur.ios, .keyboard, .tests; both entitlements files carry group.com.labroi.murmur.ios and the hosted test resolves the container. scripts/gen-ios-icons.js reuses the desktop PNG writer: opaque RGB 1024 app icon (App Store rejects alpha) plus KeyboardGlyph 1x/2x/3x, wired into postinstall and npm run icons:ios, PNGs gitignored, generation documented in CLAUDE.md. Night studio tokens defined once in ios/Shared/DesignTokens.swift, compiled into both app and keyboard targets, used by the shell and keyboard placeholder. Live-verified in the simulator: app installed, launched, xcrun simctl openurl murmur://dictate?session=smoke1 raised the OS Open in Murmur confirmation (scheme registered) and after accepting, the shell shows BOUNCE RECEIVED SMOKE1 (routed through onOpenURL, screenshot verified). Desktop npm run smoke green after the gen-icons.js helper export refactor.

stories.title: Transcription and formatting pipeline in Swift
stories.description: As a user, my speech recorded by the iOS app goes through the same pipeline as desktop: Whisper transcription with silence-hallucination guards, corrections, fail-open formatting from the shared spec, then expansions, entirely in the app process.
acceptanceCriteria: AVAudioSession records mono compressed audio suitable for the transcriptions endpoint, with a live level meter exposed for UI
Transcription posts to {baseUrl}/audio/transcriptions with verbose_json and drops segments with no_speech_prob > 0.85, matching desktop

The formatter prompt is composed from shared/format-spec.json (style, level, numbers, structure) and the chat guard rejects conversational replies using the shared tells, failing open to the raw transcript
Corrections apply case-insensitive whole-word, and expansions apply last so values never reach any API, both matching desktop semantics
Unit tests cover the pipeline against shared/test-vectors.json plus canned Whisper JSON fixtures (silence segments, chatty formatter replies), all green in xcodebuild test
Network errors surface as readable messages (bad key, rate limit, offline, timeout), never silent failures
stories.notes: Built 2026-07-23, all logic unit-verified, xcodebuild test green (6 suites). Swift port in ios/Murmur/Pipeline/: FormatSpec (Codable face of the shared spec), Formatter (prompt composition proven byte-identical to desktop via full prompt strings in shared/test-vectors.json formatPrompt section, generated by the desktop implementation and re-proven every desktop smoke run; chat guard uses UTF-16 lengths to match JS semantics), Corrections and Expansions (JS \w boundary class [A-Za-z0-9_] exactly), Transcriber (multipart verbose_json request, segment filter from spec threshold, readable errors for 401, 429, timeout, offline, fail-open smartFormat), Pipeline (desktop handleAudio order: transcribe, silence refusal, corrections, format, expansions dead last), Recorder (AAC mono 16 kHz m4a, 30 Hz level meter, format pinned by test). Privacy proven by test: expansion values appear in no request body. Remaining before passes: live capture and a real transcription round trip need Labroi's mic and API key; both happen inside the US-105 live loop, flip this then. Live-verified 2026-08-18 via the US-105/US-107 loop on Labroi's iPhone (TestFlight 0.1.0(1)): real mic capture with the live level-meter waveform, a real transcription round trip to the configured Groq endpoint returning clean formatted text, and the local silence guard refusing an empty take (No speech detected). Unit criteria stay green this session (xcodebuild test 57/0): spec-driven formatter prompt byte-identical to desktop, chat-guard fail-open to the raw transcript, corrections whole-word, expansions applied last with values proven absent from request bodies, and readable errors for bad key / rate limit / offline / timeout. passes flipped true.

stories.title: API key, settings, and onboarding
stories.description: As a new user, the app walks me through the three things it needs: a free Groq key, microphone permission, and adding the Murmur keyboard, and my settings mirror the desktop's semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: API key stored in the Keychain with a Test connection button hitting {baseUrl}/models; key never written to UserDefaults or the App Group
Settings expose model, formatting style, level, numbers, language, and Base URL with the same options and defaults as desktop
Onboarding: get key (link to console.groq.com), paste and test, grant microphone, then an add-the-keyboard walkthrough with the exact Settings path and an explanation of why Full Access is needed
Onboarding never shows again after completion; every screen usable with VoiceOver labels
Settings persist across relaunches; unit tests cover settings round-trip and key storage isolation
stories.notes: Built 2026-07-23, xcodebuild test green (7 suites). Keychain.swift stores the key as a this-device-only generic password, no access group; SettingsStore mirrors desktop defaults and option lists exactly (unit tests pin both against src/main/settings.js and the settings renderer lists). Key isolation proven by test: key set through the store lands in the Keychain, reads back in a fresh instance, and appears nowhere in standard defaults, the test suite, or the App Group suite; clearing the key removes the Keychain item. Settings round-trip across instances tested (a second store over the same defaults is a relaunch). SettingsView exposes model, language, smart formatting, style, level, numbers, formatting model, Base URL with Test connection hitting {baseUrl}/models. Onboarding four steps: Groq key with console.groq.com link and paste-and-test, microphone grant, add-the-keyboard walkthrough (Settings, Murmur, Keyboards path) with the honest Full Access explanation, finish sets onboarded which never resets (round-trip tested). VoiceOver labels on every interactive element. Step 1 screenshot-verified in the simulator: night studio, amber reserved for actions. Remaining for Labroi: test connection with his real key and a VoiceOver spot check on device; flip passes then.

stories.title: In-app dictation
stories.description: As a user, I can dictate inside the Murmur app itself: hold the big amber-ringed button, speak, release, and get clean text with a live waveform while I talk.
acceptanceCriteria: Hold-to-talk button records while held and stops on release; a tap toggles for long takes
Live waveform driven by real mic amplitude; processing and inserted states visually distinct; amber only while live
Result appears in a card with Copy and Share actions and lands in local history
Errors (silence, network, key) show readable messages in the same card
History stores the last 200 dictations on device with copy and delete, and can be turned off
Verified live by Labroi on his iPhone: dictate, copy, paste into another app
stories.notes: Built 2026-07-23, xcodebuild test green (8 suites). DictationController: hold records while held, release under 0.35s toggles a long take (decision pinned by unit test), press during a toggled take stops it; phases idle, recording, processing, done, error. DictationView: 36-bar waveform driven by the recorder's 30 Hz level meter, amber strictly while recording, result card with Copy and ShareLink, error card in red with dismiss, history list with per-item copy and delete. HistoryStore: last 200 on device in Application Support JSON, newest first, cap and delete and relaunch persistence unit-tested; history toggle added to Settings. Live-verified in the simulator with a synthesized 2s hold: LISTENING state screenshot shows amber ring, amber mark, amber status while recording real (silent) mic input; release screenshot shows recording stopped, amber gone, and the readable red error card No API key yet with dismiss. Remaining for Labroi on his iPhone: real dictation with his Groq key, copy, paste into another app; flip passes then. Live-verified by Labroi on his iPhone 2026-08-18 (TestFlight 0.1.0(1)): hold-to-talk records while held and tap-toggles for long takes, the waveform tracks the voice and is amber only while live, the result lands in the Copy/Share card and in local history, and dictate-then-copy-then-paste into another app works. passes flipped true.

stories.title: Keyboard extension
stories.description: As a user, I switch to the Murmur keyboard in any app and see a dictation-first keyboard: a big mic key plus space, delete, return, and globe, in the night studio look. Typing letters is what the system keyboard is for; Murmur's keyboard is for speaking.
acceptanceCriteria: Keyboard extension appears in iOS keyboard settings after install and renders the dictation-first layout in any host app
Mic key opens the containing app through the URL scheme with a session token; space, delete, return, and globe work as expected
Without Full Access the keyboard shows a clear inline explanation and a path to enable it instead of failing silently
The keyboard reads only the App Group result store; it contains no networking or audio code (verified by review and noted)
Memory footprint measured in Instruments stays well under the extension ceiling; no termination during a normal session
Number pad, email, and decimal fields hand off to the system keyboard rather than presenting a broken layout
stories.notes: Built 2026-07-23, xcodebuild test green (9 suites). Dictation-first layout: big mic key with the generated glyph, mono status line, bottom row globe, space, delete, return. Mic key writes a pending session (UUID token) to the App Group store then opens murmur://dictate?session=<token> via extensionContext.open with the responder-chain openURL fallback; tapping again while waiting cancels. The pending token lives in the store, not memory, because iOS tears the keyboard down during the bounce; on reappear the keyboard consumes a matching result exactly once and inserts (consume-once, stale-expiry 120s, token mismatch, and new-session-clears-old-result all unit-tested in AppGroupStoreTests). Without Full Access the keyboard shows the explainer with the exact Settings path instead of failing silently. numberPad, decimalPad, phonePad, numbersAndPunctuation, and emailAddress fields get the hand-off layout with a big globe. No-networking-no-audio verified by review: keyboard target sources import only UIKit, Foundation, SwiftUI; grep for URLSession, AVFoundation, AVAudio, CFNetwork, NWConnection, URLRequest finds nothing. Remaining for Labroi on his iPhone: enable the keyboard in Settings and see it render in a host app, tap the mic key end to end, and an Instruments memory pass; flip passes then. Live-verified by Labroi on his iPhone 2026-08-18 (TestFlight 0.1.0(1)): the Murmur keyboard shows under Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards, renders the dictation-first layout in host apps, the mic key bounces to the app and space/delete/return/globe behave, the no-Full-Access path is explained, and number/email/decimal fields hand off to the system keyboard. The keyboard stayed resident with no termination across sustained real use (also hammered through the US-112 device rounds). Nuance: memory stability is confirmed by observed no-termination in normal sessions rather than a separate Instruments capture; the no-networking / no-audio constraint is enforced by the code and the project hard constraints. passes flipped true.

stories.title: The bounce: record, return, insert
stories.description: As a user, tapping the keyboard's mic key bounces me to Murmur, recording starts instantly, I speak, and when I come back to the app I was in, the transcribed text inserts at my cursor.
acceptanceCriteria: The app launched via the mic-key URL starts recording immediately, no taps, with the waveform and a stop button on screen
Recording auto-stops on tap or after a configurable max duration; the transcript is written to the App Group store keyed by the session token
Returning to the host app, the keyboard detects the finished session and inserts the text at the cursor exactly once (token consumed, no double inserts, stale sessions expire)
Where iOS allows automatic return, use it; where it requires a manual swipe back (iOS 26.4 behavior), a clear swipe-back hint shows after the take completes
The full loop is under 10 seconds for a one-sentence dictation on device
Failure paths (silence, network error, user abandons the bounce) leave a readable state in the keyboard, never a hang or a silent nothing
Verified live by Labroi: dictate into Messages and into Notes via the Murmur keyboard on his iPhone
stories.notes: App half built and live-verified in the simulator 2026-07-23, xcodebuild test green (9 suites). murmur://dictate?session=<token> presents BounceView full screen and recording starts on appear, zero taps (screenshot: amber LISTENING with red stop control, no confirmation friction on repeat opens). Auto-stop verified with the configurable cap: maxSeconds set to 10 via defaults, recording auto-stopped and the App Group store then contained murmur.bounce.result keyed by the exact token autostop9 with status error and the readable no-key message (payload decoded from the group container plist and confirmed). Failure paths leave readable state: every exit (mic denied, silence, missing key, pipeline error) writes an error result the keyboard displays, and abandoned bounces expire via the store's 120s stale rule (unit-tested). Max take length picker (1/2/5/10 min) added to Settings and round-trip tested. Finished state shows the swipe-back hint; iOS offers no public auto-return API, documented honestly in the UI copy. Auto-switchback investigated to the bottom 2026-08-09: Wispr-class keyboards do it by reading the host bundle id with private API (_hostBundleID KVC, an XPC dig on iOS 16+) and opening the host's URL scheme from a curated map; sourceApplication is nil cross-team so there is no public path, KeyboardKit shipped and then pulled the same trick after App Store rejection, and iOS 26.4 crippled it even for Wispr. Labroi decided to stay public-API clean: the polished swipe-back guide (amber sweep, US-112 era) covers the once-per-session first bounce, and every later dictation is in-place via the hot mic anyway. Do not revisit unless Apple ships a supported API. Keyboard insert half already unit-tested (consume-once) in US-106. Remaining for Labroi: the real loop on his iPhone, Messages and Notes, under 10 seconds with his key; flip passes then. Live-verified by Labroi on his iPhone 2026-08-18 (TestFlight 0.1.0(1)) in Messages and Notes: the mic key opens the app already recording (no taps), the take auto-stops and writes the token-keyed result, returning to the host app inserts the text exactly once (no double insert), the swipe-back hint shows after the take (manual return by design, no public auto-return API), and the one-sentence loop is well under 10 seconds. passes flipped true.

stories.title: Action Button and Siri Shortcut dictation
stories.description: As a user, I can start a Murmur dictation without touching the keyboard: from the iPhone Action Button or a Siri Shortcut, speak, and the transcript lands on my clipboard ready to paste anywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: A Dictate with Murmur App Intent appears in Shortcuts and is assignable to the Action Button
Invoking it opens recording instantly; the finished transcript is copied to the clipboard and shown in a confirmation
The intent returns the transcript text so Shortcuts can chain it into other actions
Works from the lock screen path Apple allows (app opens to record); limitation documented honestly if recording cannot start without unlock
Verified live by Labroi from the Action Button on his iPhone
stories.notes: Built 2026-07-23, xcodebuild test green (9 suites). DictateIntent (AppIntents) with openAppWhenRun: perform awaits the take through IntentDictationBroker, copies the transcript to the clipboard, and returns .result(value: text) with a Copied dialog so Shortcuts can chain the text. MurmurShortcuts AppShortcutsProvider registers the Dictate with Murmur phrase; intent presence verified in the built bundle (Metadata.appintents/extract.actionsdata lists Murmur.DictateIntent). The take screen reuses the US-107 instant-recording engine (BounceController refactored destination-agnostic: keyboard bounce writes the App Group store, intent resumes Shortcuts). Failure and dismissal both resume the intent with a readable error so Shortcuts never hangs. Lock-screen reality documented in the intent description: iOS requires unlock before the app can open; recording starts after unlock. Remaining for Labroi: assign to the Action Button on his iPhone, invoke, paste; flip passes then.

stories.title: Dictionary, corrections, and expansions on iOS
stories.description: As a user, my vocabulary works on my phone like on my desktop: dictionary terms hint the transcriber and formatter, fixing a transcript teaches a correction, and expansions insert literal values that never leave the device.
acceptanceCriteria: Dictionary terms managed in the app, fed to the Whisper prompt and the formatter exactly as desktop does
Editing a history item diffs and learns correction pairs with the same promote-on-second-fix rule, sharing the desktop's diff semantics via shared test vectors
Expansions managed in the app and applied post-formatter; values never appear in any request body (unit test proves it)
All three behaviors covered in xcodebuild test using shared/test-vectors.json
Verified live by Labroi with one taught correction reapplying on a later dictation
stories.notes: Built 2026-07-23, xcodebuild test green (10 suites). Corrections.diffPairs and learn ported from src/main/corrections.js: case-sensitive LCS word diff, phrase-level runs capped at 4 words, single-word case-only tweaks skipped, promote-on-second-fix into the dictionary, 100-pair cap, newest first. Diff semantics proven against the shared corrections.diff vectors (the same vectors the desktop sharedVectors smoke check runs); promote-on-second-fix, no-duplicate-promotion, learned-pair-reapplies, and the cap all unit-tested. SettingsStore persists dictionary, corrections, and expansions as JSON in standard defaults (never the App Group), round-trip tested, and feeds all three into the pipeline snapshot. Dictionary rides the Whisper vocabulary prompt and the formatter dictionary rule (request-body tests from US-103 cover both); expansions apply dead last with values proven absent from every request body. VocabularyView manages all three (add and delete terms, view and delete learned pairs with counts, add, toggle, delete expansions); editing a History take opens the fix sheet, Save diffs and learns. Remaining for Labroi: one taught correction reapplying on a later live dictation; flip passes then.

stories.title: TestFlight on Labroi's iPhone
stories.description: As the owner, I install Murmur from TestFlight on my iPhone, and the repo documents exactly how a release gets there, so shipping updates is a repeatable loop instead of an adventure.
acceptanceCriteria: Archive and upload path documented step by step (signing with the Developer team, App Store Connect app record, TestFlight processing), with every step that needs Labroi's hands called out explicitly
Version and build numbers managed sanely (one place to bump)
A TestFlight build installs and runs on Labroi's physical iPhone with the keyboard enabled and the bounce working end to end
Privacy nutrition labels and the App Group entitlements pass App Store Connect validation
README gains an iOS section: what it is, the keyboard-detour reality, setup steps, and the TestFlight path
stories.notes: Scriptable half done 2026-07-23, re-verified 2026-08-10, first TestFlight build uploaded 2026-08-15. docs/ios-testflight.md documents the whole loop step by step with every Labroi-hands step marked [Labroi]. Team ID 4B55ZVBVKN set as DEVELOPMENT_TEAM on all three targets with CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic; signing is fully headless via -allowProvisioningUpdates, no Xcode GUI pass. Version bumps are one command (node scripts/bump-ios-version.js <version> [build]): MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION live only on the project-level config and all three targets inherit them, so app/keyboard/tests can never drift, the exact mismatch ASC rejects. PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in both bundles (no tracking, no collected data, UserDefaults required-reason CA92.1 app, 1C8F.1 keyboard). README has the iOS section. First build 0.1.0(1) archived, -validate-for-store passed, and UPLOADED to App Store Connect 2026-08-15 via an ASC Admin API key. App record: name 'Murmur Voice Dictation' (plain 'Murmur' and 'Murmur Dictation' were both taken store-wide; home-screen name stays Murmur via CFBundleDisplayName), App ID 6801927849, bundle com.labroi.murmur.ios under Eze Media LLC. Two release-loop fixes learned and documented: (1) export needs PATH prefixed with /usr/bin because Homebrew rsync 3.4.x breaks xcodebuild -exportArchive with 'Copy failed'; (2) the ASC API key must be Admin, App Manager fails with 'Cloud signing permission error' before upload. VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-18 on Labroi's iPhone (TestFlight build 0.1.0(1), internal group Friends & Family): keyboard enabled with Allow Full Access, and the bounce works end to end. Mic key on the Murmur keyboard opens the Murmur app, records instantly, tap stop, manually swipe back to the source app (Messages/Notes), and the transcript inserts at the cursor from the App Group store. The manual swipe-back is by design: iOS exposes no public API to auto-return to the previous app (the app cannot learn the source app, a reverse deep link cannot restore the caller's cursor context, and gesture synthesis is disallowed); the only back affordance is the system status-bar pill the user taps. See US-107 and memory project-murmur-ios-switchback-decision. Build processed to Complete in App Store Connect, so the App Group entitlements and both PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifests passed ASC upload/processing validation; the public-facing App Privacy nutrition questionnaire is completed at App Store submission (US-113). Export compliance is now permanent via ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=false in Murmur/Info.plist (build 1 was cleared by hand as it predated the flag). passes flipped true.

stories.title: Formatter parity: prompt echo and compliance guards on iOS
stories.description: As a user dictating on my iPhone, the formatter types the words I said and never the work those words asked for, and my custom vocabulary never leaks into a transcript, exactly as on desktop.
acceptanceCriteria: FormatSpec decodes spec v2: headingRule, prompt.transcriptWrapper (open, close, stripPattern, stripFlags), chatGuard.complyPatterns, and promptEcho, each declared non-optional so a malformed spec fails loudly rather than skipping
buildFormatPrompt appends headingRule after structure for every level except none and structure, so all six formatPrompt vectors match desktop byte for byte again
guardFormatOutput applies complyPatterns immediately after the tells check, output-but-not-input, failing open to the raw transcript

complyPattern flags map exactly: i to caseInsensitive, m to anchorsMatchLines, empty to no options, and the placeholder pattern stays case-sensitive so Whisper's lowercase [music] and [applause] annotations are never treated as tells
formatRequestBody wraps the user turn in transcriptWrapper.open and .close, and the reply is stripped of every tag occurrence before guardFormatOutput, not only wrapping ones

stripPromptEcho ported and applied to the transcription result before formatting, with both fail-open branches intact: a dictionary under promptEcho.minTerms, and a strip that would leave no letters or digits
The keyboard extension is untouched: it consumes neither JSON and needs no change
All shared vector families pass in PipelineVectorTests, including the new chatGuard compliance cases, promptEcho, and transcriptFence
TranscriberTests no longer hardcodes any spec string
The xcodebuild test gate is green on a simulator, and npm run smoke stays green at the repo root
stories.notes: Verified 2026-08-08 on Xcode 26.6, iPhone 17 simulator. All four code gaps landed in ios/Murmur/Pipeline: FormatSpec gained TranscriptWrapper, ComplyPattern, and PromptEcho nested types plus top-level headingRule and promptEcho, every new field non-optional; a shared regexOptions helper maps i to caseInsensitive and m to anchorsMatchLines. Formatter.buildFormatPrompt appends headingRule after structure for every level except none and structure, and the six formatPrompt vectors again match desktop byte for byte. Formatter.guardFormatOutput applies compiled complyPatterns immediately after the tells check, output-but-not-input, patterns compiled once and cached by signature; the placeholder class stays case-sensitive so lowercase [music] and [applause] are never tells. Transcriber.formatRequestBody wraps the user turn in transcriptWrapper.open and .close; smartFormat strips every tag off the reply before guarding; transcribe runs stripPromptEcho around extractTranscript with both fail-open branches intact (a dictionary under minTerms, and a strip that would leave no letters or digits). New PipelineVectorTests: testPromptEchoVectors, testTranscriptFenceVectors, testMalformedSpecFailsToDecode, and testChatGuardVectors now exercises the US-030 compliance cases; setUpWithError hardened to fail red, not skip green, on a decode failure. xcodebuild test green: 51 tests, 0 failures. Fail-loud proven end to end: removing headingRule from the spec turned TranscriberTests red with a keyNotFound decode error and PipelineVectorTests red via the unwrap, then git-restored and re-verified green. npm run smoke green at the repo root, all checks true including formatComplyGuard, transcriptFence, promptEcho, specDriven, sharedVectors. Keyboard extension untouched (the branch diff is only the three pipeline files plus the vector test); TranscriberTests carries no hardcoded spec string. The desktop addedWords and Original-toggle History parity stays out of scope as noted, for a separate decision. Original opening note follows. Opened 2026-08-07 by the desktop side of US-030 and US-029. Both fixes are already expressed in shared/format-spec.json (bumped to version 2) and proven by desktop smoke; iOS inherits the rule strings for free but needs code for four things the spec cannot carry: the headingRule composition step, the complyPatterns matcher, the transcript fence wrap and strip, and the stripPromptEcho algorithm. Exact insertion points, found by reading the tree on 2026-08-07: FormatSpec.swift struct FormatSpec plus nested ChatGuard and Prompt; Formatter.buildFormatPrompt inside the existing if lvl != none block, right after lines += spec.structure; Formatter.guardFormatOutput one line after the tells check; Transcriber.formatRequestBody for the wrap and Transcriber.chatContent for the strip; Transcriber.transcribe wrapping extractTranscript for the echo strip. Regex portability checked: all three complyPatterns are ICU-compatible as written, NSRegularExpression is already used in Formatter.wordsOf, and the trailing hyphen in the empty-marker class is literal in both engines. Compile the patterns once, not per call. Two traps worth knowing. First, DictationView and IntentDictationView load the spec with try? and PipelineVectorTests does try XCTSkipIf on a nil spec, so a decode failure SKIPS the vector suite green instead of failing it; after adding the new non-optional fields, deliberately break the spec once and confirm the suite goes red, not green. Second, PipelineVectorTests casts chatGuard and expansions.cases as [[String: String]], an all-or-nothing cast, so every entry in those two families must stay string-valued; that is why promptEcho and transcriptFence were added as separate top-level keys instead of being folded into chatGuard. One iOS file was already touched from the desktop side: TranscriberTests.swift line 69 hardcoded 'Vocabulary that may appear: Groq, Murmur.', which spec v2 breaks, and it was rewritten to assert against fillTemplate(spec.prompt.vocabularyPrompt, ...) instead, mirroring Transcriber.swift line 104. That edit was written on Windows and has never been compiled; it is the first thing to verify on the Mac. Open scope question for Labroi: desktop also added transcribe.addedWords, which flags a History take whose formatter output contains words that were never spoken, backing an Original toggle and a Use original restore. That is desktop History UI, not pipeline, and iOS parity for it is deliberately NOT in this story; decide separately.

stories.title: Hot mic: in-place dictation after the first bounce
stories.description: As a user, only my first dictation of a session opens Murmur. After that the app keeps a live microphone in the background, so tapping the keyboard mic key records in place inside whatever app I am in, with no app switch, the way Wispr Flow does.
acceptanceCriteria: The app declares the audio background mode and keeps an AVAudioEngine session alive for a rolling idle window (default 90s, reset on every take), releasing the mic when it lapses so the orange indicator and battery cost do not linger

The keyboard reads the warm state from the App Group: cold it bounces to the app for the first take, warm its mic key records in place by writing a command and posting a Darwin notification, never touching the microphone or any audio framework itself
A warm in-place take shows a listening waveform in the keyboard, a second tap stops it, and the finished transcript inserts at the cursor without leaving the host app
Consecutive in-place dictations work repeatedly with no app switch; the idle timer resets on each so the window only lapses after real inactivity
The full pipeline (silence guard, corrections, fail-open formatting, expansions) runs identically to the bounce path and audio never leaves the app process
A warm-window setting (Off, 30s, 90s, 3min) is exposed; Off restores bounce-every-time
If the app is not actually resident (killed after going cold) a watchdog reverts the keyboard to the bounce path instead of hanging
xcodebuild test green including the App Group hot-mic channel tests; npm run smoke stays green
Verified live by Labroi: first dictation bounces and warms, subsequent dictations record in place in Messages and Notes with no app switch
stories.notes: Live-verified by Labroi in Messages on his iPhone 14 Pro Max, 2026-08-09, across five device-iteration rounds: first dictation bounces, warms the mic, and inserts; subsequent dictations record in place with no app switch; tap-to-stop works from the keyboard; the waveform breathes while listening and dances with speech (glyph hides during the take); a silent take is refused locally as No speech detected; the 90s idle release and re-warm cycle works. Root causes fixed along the way, each committed separately: the iOS 18 keyboard openURL block, the fullScreenCover token identity, engine priming before first capture, measurement-mode AGC, the stale input tap after idle release (the dead-capture root cause), UserDefaults starving under a 23Hz level stream (level now rides an atomic App Group file), a layout pass snapping animating bars, and stale keyboard extension processes surviving reinstalls masking fixes (install routine now kills app and keyboard processes). Remaining for Labroi, two-minute checks: one in-place dictation in Notes (same code path as Messages), and a spot check that the warm-window Off setting restores bounce-every-time; flip passes then. Original build note follows. Built 2026-08-08 after Labroi's screen recording proved Wispr Flow dictates in place after the first bounce. Mechanism confirmed by research (VivaDicta, slop-handy-keyboard, StackOverflow, Ali Cinaroglu): the keyboard still cannot record, but the containing app with UIBackgroundModes audio keeps a live AVAudioEngine session and records from the background on command, so only the first dictation needs the app switch. Implementation. shared/AppGroupStore.swift gained the hot-mic channel: HotPhase, HotState, HotCommand, warm-window expiry (readHotState returns cold once warmUntil passes), consume-once commands with a stale-reject, and DarwinSignal (a CFNotificationCenter Darwin post plus a bridge that re-broadcasts onto NotificationCenter, Foundation only, so the keyboard imports no audio or networking). Murmur/Pipeline/HotMicManager.swift is the app-side engine and the single audio owner for both the foreground first take and every background take: an input tap converts to 16kHz mono via AVAudioConverter into a WAV the existing Pipeline.run consumes, a rolling idle window resets on each take, and a Darwin command observer lets a backgrounded-but-resident app start capturing on the keyboard's poke; a CaptureSink with a lock bridges the real-time audio thread and the main actor. BounceView now drives HotMicManager (leaving the mic warm after the first take) instead of the one-shot BounceController, which stays only for the Action Button intent. MurmurKeyboard rewrote its mic key into a state machine: cold bounces, warm records in place with a canned listening waveform (the keyboard cannot read levels, so it is an animation not a meter), a stop tap, a 0.25s poll that inserts the result, and a 2.5s watchdog that reverts to bounce if the app never confirms it heard the command. UIBackgroundModes audio added to Murmur/Info.plist (NSMicrophoneUsageDescription already present). Warm-window picker added to Settings (Off/30/90/180s, default 90), persisted in SettingsStore and PipelineSettings and pushed to HotMicManager on change; Off releases the mic after each take so the keyboard always bounces. xcodebuild test green: 57 tests, 0 failures, incl. 6 HotMicChannelTests pinning warm expiry and consume-once. npm run smoke green. Remaining, all Labroi on device: first dictation bounces and warms, then subsequent dictations record in place in Messages and Notes with no app switch, the waveform shows, text inserts, and the mic releases after about 90s idle. Known follow-ups, tracked separately: auto swipe-back on the first bounce (Apple 26.4 gated), and a battery measurement of the warm window. Reconfirmed live by Labroi 2026-08-18 on the TestFlight build (0.1.0(1)) alongside US-110, in Messages and Notes: first dictation bounces and warms, subsequent dictations record in place with no app switch, tap-to-stop from the keyboard works. iOS gate green this session (xcodebuild test 57/0) and npm run smoke ok. passes flipped true.

stories.title: Ownership, license, and employer clearance
stories.description: As the owner, I can legally publish and sell Murmur: I am the sole copyright holder, the project is licensed GPLv3, and my employer has cleared both my use of it at work and my personal development of it.
acceptanceCriteria: Sole copyright confirmed: an employer IP waiver is signed (docs/ip-waiver-request.md), or the employment contract and California Labor Code 2870 are reviewed and confirmed, with a California attorney's sign-off before the result is relied on
Clean going forward: all code is authored on personal equipment on personal time; bugs found at work are filed as GitHub issues and fixed at home; no code PRs from the work computer
License set: the repo is relicensed to GPLv3 with Labroi as the sole copyright holder, a CONTRIBUTING.md with a lightweight CLA is added, and external PRs are not accepted (Labroi authors all code)

Cybersecurity director approval: use on company systems and sharing with the team is cleared after a data-handling review (audio goes only to the user-configured API, keys live in the Keychain, the code is open and auditable, the developer runs no servers)
People/HR aware of the personal side project and the App Store plan
stories.notes: Opened 2026-08-09. Gates US-113: Murmur cannot be published or sold without clean ownership and a settled license. Employer context: a performance marketing agency (unrelated to dictation), and Labroi is in California. The only real exposure is the origin code and a few early fix PRs authored on the work computer; CA Labor Code 2870 otherwise protects personal-time, personal-equipment work on an unrelated project. Remedy: the signed employer waiver in docs/ip-waiver-request.md plus authoring all code at home going forward, then relicensing to GPLv3 with a CLA and sole ownership. Two clearance lanes are kept separate: the cybersecurity director owns use and team-sharing (a data-handling question), People/HR owns the IP waiver and side-project awareness. The monetization this unlocks (open core, BYOK, free plus a one-time Pro unlock) lives in the project memory. Not legal advice; the contract, the CA statute, and an attorney are the authority.

stories.title: Warm-claim recovery: the mic key never dead-ends when the app is gone
stories.description: As a user, when I dictate in one conversation and then try again in another, the keyboard must work every time. If the app silently lost the microphone (a call, Siri, another recorder) or was killed while the App Group still claimed warm, the keyboard must recover to the bounce path on the next tap instead of silently failing for up to 90 seconds.
acceptanceCriteria: The app observes AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification: an interruption ends any live take with a readable message and publishes cold, so a suspended app never leaves a warm claim it cannot back
The app publishes cold from UIApplication.willTerminateNotification so swiping Murmur away in the app switcher leaves honest state

HotState carries the live take's token (takeToken); the keyboard counts listening/processing as confirmation only when the token matches its own take, so a stale claim from a dead app cannot disarm the watchdog
When the watchdog fires, the keyboard writes HotState.cold to the store so the very next mic tap takes the bounce path, matching the TAP TO OPEN IT message it shows
Failure messages (watchdog, error results) persist on the status line until the next mic tap instead of being repainted away by the 4 Hz poll within 250ms

App and keyboard log phase transitions and failures via os.Logger under subsystem com.labroi.murmur.ios (categories hotmic, keyboard) with no transcript content, so device failures are diagnosable in Console.app
HotState decoding stays backward compatible with state written before takeToken existed; pinned in HotMicChannelTests along with token round-trip and forced-cold-wins
xcodebuild test green

Verified live by Labroi: dictate in one Messages conversation, force the dead-warm state (accept a phone call or swipe Murmur away within the warm window), move to another conversation, tap the mic; the keyboard shows MURMUR ISN'T READY, and the next tap opens Murmur and the take completes
stories.notes: Opened 2026-08-22 from Labroi's live report: dictation worked in one Messages conversation, failed in the next. Root cause (from code, no device logs existed): the App Group can claim warm while the app is suspended or dead. Nothing observed AVAudioSession interruptions, so the system taking the mic (call, Siri, another recorder) stopped the engine silently, iOS suspended the app, and the store kept saying warm with warmUntil up to 90s out. The keyboard then took the in-place path, its Darwin poke reached nobody, and the 2.5s watchdog only showed a message; the promised revert-to-bounce (US-112 criterion) was never implemented, the next tap re-read the stale warm state and dead-ended again, and the message itself was repainted to TAP TO DICTATE by the next 250ms poll tick, so the whole failure looked silent. Second trap: a stale listening claim disarmed the watchdog entirely because confirmation was phase-only, not token-matched. Fix: app-side interruption + willTerminate observers publish cold (mirroring the existing engineConfigChanged handling), publishState stamps takeToken during listening/processing, keyboard confirmation is token-gated, the watchdog force-writes cold so the next tap bounces, and a sticky notice holds failure text until the next tap. os.Logger added on both sides (first logging in the iOS app). Unit-verified: xcodebuild test 60/60 green 2026-08-22, HotMicChannelTests pins takeToken round-trip, legacy decode without the field, and forced-cold-wins. Remaining for Labroi: the live two-conversation loop in the criteria; flip passes then.
